nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and all coprime $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Entry 30 coefficients $c_a$ satisfy $c_a(mn) = c_a(m)\,c_a(n)$.
nodes.title: Entry 30 coefficients are multiplicative

nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ne 0$, the Entry 30 coefficient $c_a(n)$ equals the product of $a(p)$ over the prime factors $p$ of $n$ when $n$ is squarefree, and $c_a(n) = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Closed form of the Entry 30 coefficients

nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every natural number $n \ne 0$ that is not squarefree, the Entry 30 coefficient $c_a(n)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Entry 30 coefficients vanish at nonzero non-squarefree natural numbers

nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every squarefree $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ne 0$, the Entry 30 coefficient $c_a(n)$ is the product of $a(p)$ over the prime factors $p$ of $n$.
nodes.title: Entry 30 coefficients at squarefree integers

nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$, the Entry 30 coefficient $c_a(1)$ is $1$.
nodes.title: The Entry 30 coefficient at one

nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$, every prime $p$ and every $e \ge 2$, the Entry 30 coefficient satisfies $c_a(p^e) = 0$.
nodes.title: Entry 30 coefficients vanish at higher prime powers

nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every prime $p$, the Entry 30 coefficient $c_a(p)$ equals $a(p)$.
nodes.title: Entry 30 coefficients at primes

nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$, the Entry 30 coefficient $c_a(0)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The Entry 30 coefficient at zero

nodes.summary: For a function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Entry 30 coefficient $c_a(n) \in \mathbb{C}$ is $0$ when $n = 0$. When $n \ne 0$ it is the product, over the prime factors $p$ of $n$, of the local factor of $a$ at $p$ with exponent the multiplicity of $p$ in $n$. The local factor at $p$ with exponent $e$ is $1$ for $e = 0$, $a(p)$ for $e = 1$, and $0$ for $e \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Coefficients for Entry 30

nodes.summary: For every function $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$, every $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $e \ge 2$, the Entry 30 local factor of $a$ at $p$ with exponent $e$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Entry 30 local factors vanish at exponents at least two

nodes.summary: For every $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every natural number $p$, the local factor of $a$ at $p$ with exponent $1$ is $a(p)$.
nodes.title: Local factor at exponent one

nodes.summary: For every $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every natural number $p$, the local factor of $a$ at $p$ with exponent $0$ is $1$.
nodes.title: Local factor at exponent zero

nodes.summary: Given $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and natural numbers $p$ and $e$, the local factor of $a$ at $p$ with exponent $e$ is $1$ if $e = 0$, $a(p)$ if $e = 1$, and $0$ if $e \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Local factor

nodes.summary: For $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a natural number $j$, the $j$-th term of the Dirichlet series over non-squarefree integers equals $0$ if $j + 1$ is squarefree and $(j + 1)^{-s}$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Non-squarefree term, explicit form

nodes.summary: For $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a natural number $j$, put $n = j + 1$; the $j$-th term is $0$ if $n$ is squarefree and $n^{-s}$ otherwise. As $j$ ranges over the natural numbers, these are the terms of $\sum n^{-s}$ over non-squarefree $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Terms of the Dirichlet series over non-squarefree integers

nodes.summary: For $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a natural number $j$, the $j$-th term of the Dirichlet series over squarefree integers with an odd number of prime factors equals $(j + 1)^{-s}$ if $j + 1$ is squarefree and has an odd number of distinct prime factors, and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Odd-count squarefree term, explicit form

nodes.summary: For $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a natural number $j$, put $n = j + 1$; the $j$-th term is $n^{-s}$ if $n$ is squarefree and has an odd number of distinct prime factors, and $0$ otherwise. As $j$ ranges over the natural numbers, these are the terms of $\sum n^{-s}$ over squarefree $n \ge 1$ with an odd number of prime factors.
nodes.title: Terms over squarefree integers with an odd number of prime factors

nodes.summary: For $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a natural number $n \ne 0$, the signed coefficient of $n$ equals $-n^{-s}$ if $n$ is squarefree with an odd number of distinct prime factors, $n^{-s}$ if $n$ is squarefree with an even number of distinct prime factors, and $0$ if $n$ is not squarefree.
nodes.title: Explicit form of the signed coefficient

nodes.summary: For $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a natural number $n$, let $a(p) = -p^{-s}$ for natural numbers $p$. The signed coefficient of $n$ is $0$ if $n = 0$ and, for $n \ne 0$, the product over the prime factors $p$ of $n$ of the local factor of $a$ at $p$ with exponent the multiplicity of $p$ in $n$, where the local factor of $a$ at $p$ with exponent $e$ is $1$ for $e = 0$, $a(p)$ for $e = 1$, and $0$ for $e \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Signed multiplicative coefficient

nodes.summary: For $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a natural number $j$, the $j$-th term of the Dirichlet series over squarefree integers equals $(j + 1)^{-s}$ if $j + 1$ is squarefree and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Squarefree term, explicit form

nodes.summary: For a complex number $s$ and a natural number $j$, let $n = j + 1$; the $j$-th squarefree term is $n^{-s}$ if $n$ is squarefree and $0$ otherwise, so the series of these terms over $j \ge 0$ is $\sum n^{-s}$ over the squarefree $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Terms of the Dirichlet series over squarefree integers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $N$, the largest size of a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab$ is not squarefree for all $a, b \in A$ (including $a = b$) is the number of integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le N$ that are even or not squarefree.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 844 is true

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, let $E_N$ be the set of integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le N$ that are even or not squarefree. The statement that for every natural number $N$, the largest size of a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab$ is not squarefree for all $a, b \in A$ (including $a = b$) is the size of $E_N$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 844

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, the set of integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le N$ that are even or not squarefree, that is, the even numbers in $\{1, \dots, N\}$ together with the odd non-squarefree numbers in $\{1, \dots, N\}$.
nodes.title: Even or odd non-squarefree numbers up to a bound

nodes.summary: Let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $c > 1$ be real with $|a(p)| \le p^{-c}$ for every prime $p$. Write $f_a(n)$ for the Entry 30 coefficient of $a$ at $n$ (it is $0$ at $n = 0$; for $n \ge 1$ it is the product of $a(p)$ over the primes $p \mid n$ if $n$ is squarefree, and $0$ otherwise). Then the product of $1 + a(p)$ over all primes $p$ converges unconditionally to $1 + \sum_{n \ge 2} f_a(n)$.
nodes.title: Euler product for the Entry 30 coefficients

nodes.summary: (i) Let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $c > 1$ be real with $|a(p)| \le p^{-c}$ for every prime $p$, and write $f_a(n)$ for the Entry 30 coefficient of $a$ at $n$. Then the family $(f_a(n))_{n \ge 2}$ is summable; for every $n \ge 1$, $f_a(n)$ is the product of $a(p)$ over the primes $p \mid n$ if $n$ is squarefree and $0$ otherwise; and the product of $1 + a(p)$ over all primes $p$ converges…
nodes.title: Ramanujan's squarefree Dirichlet series (Entry 30)

nodes.summary: Let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $c > 1$ be real with $|a(p)| \le p^{-c}$ for every prime $p$. Then the Entry 30 coefficients $f_a(n)$ of $a$ (equal to $0$ at $n = 0$; for $n \ge 1$, the product of $a(p)$ over the primes $p \mid n$ if $n$ is squarefree, and $0$ otherwise) form a summable family over $n \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Summability of the Entry 30 coefficients

nodes.summary: For every complex number $s$ with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, the series of $n^{-s}$ over the non-squarefree $n \ge 1$ is summable.
nodes.title: Summability of the non-squarefree terms

nodes.summary: For every complex number $s$ with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, the series of $n^{-s}$ over the squarefree $n \ge 1$ with an odd number of distinct prime factors is summable.
nodes.title: Summability of the odd squarefree terms

nodes.summary: For every complex number $s$ with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, the series of $n^{-s}$ over the squarefree $n \ge 1$ is summable.
nodes.title: Summability of the squarefree terms

nodes.summary: For every complex number $s$ with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, the sum of $n^{-s}$ over the non-squarefree $n \ge 1$ equals $\zeta(s)(\zeta(2s) - 1)/\zeta(2s)$.
nodes.title: Sum of $n^{-s}$ over non-squarefree $n$

nodes.summary: For every complex number $s$ with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, the sum of $n^{-s}$ over the squarefree $n \ge 1$ with an odd number of distinct prime factors equals $(\zeta(s)^2 - \zeta(2s))/(2\zeta(s)\zeta(2s))$.
nodes.title: Sum of $n^{-s}$ over squarefree $n$ with an odd number of prime factors

nodes.summary: For every complex number $s$ with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, the sum of $n^{-s}$ over the squarefree $n \ge 1$ equals $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$.
nodes.title: Sum of $n^{-s}$ over squarefree $n$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
